title: Keep ambience 8-12 dB under bed
statement: Ambience and room tone sit 8-12 dB under the bed's own K-level (or -35 to -28 LUFS-S alone), high-passed at 60 Hz: a floor, not an event.
evidence: Pack mix table; library ambiences are seamless 8 s loops meant about -10 dB re the bed.

evidence: Two tier-A round-7 films fade to -27.7 and -45.6 dB over the last 2 s; 6 of 16 round-7 films fade 2-4 s; round 8 ends on a quiet hold or decay in 6 of 8.

evidence: one tier-A film dips at 18.0-19.68 s and 21.7-22.48 s, each dip starting or ending on a cut; another film dips 1 s before its voice; round 8 also found silence used as a cue.

title: Hero hits and logos 4-6 dB over bed
statement: A hero impact, stinger or sonic logo sits +4 to +6 dB over the bed (hero default +4.5, logo +5; K-weighted over 60 ms from the anchor against the un-dipped bed), never above +6 dB so viewers do not mute after a loud first second; a logo with no bed sits about -16 LUFS-S.
evidence: Over-bed band measured by ear on an earlier launch-film mix (3-6 dB) and fixed as the pack table; no reach data.

[house; House acceptance line; measured builds passed at +3.36 to +5.23 dB with limiter reduction up to 1.32 dB.] | Without the own-level floor a solver once passed by trimming three ticks to -30 dB: look and listen, not just the table. title: Space hero hits 8-10 s apart
statement: At most one tier-1 hero hit per 8-10 s and never two within 3 s; tier-2 transition cues average at least 1.0 s apart (aim 1.5-2 s); tier-3 micro cues sit 6 dB under tier 2 and never on a tier-2 frame unless they are its layer.
evidence: Pack hierarchy rule (a film where everything hits hits nothing); not measured for reach.
notes: Conflict inside the sources: sound.md says tier 1 never within 90 frames (3 s at 30 fps) and one per 8-10 s, tier 2 one per 1.5-2 s; the mixer lint enforces looser limits (tier 1 <= one per 5 s and never within 3 s; tier 2 average >= 1.0 s). The lint values are what code checks. | Merged: Tier-1 hero hits sit at least 3 s apart with no more than one per 5 s, and tier-2 cues average at least 1.0 s apart. [house; house mixer lint R4.] | Found in music/mixer.py (issues R4). Hardware recipe: ONE sub hit on the reveal frame; a detent per spec row, never a chime per row.

title: Land hits one frame after picture
statement: A cue whose visual lands on frame F puts its designated peak on sample (F + 1) x 48000 / fps (33.3 ms late at 30 fps, 16.7 ms at 60 fps); at least 80% of measurable cues sit within 0.5 frame of that anchor.
evidence: Pack contract from an earlier launch-film pipeline, judged best by ear; ears found 64 of 64 mixer-placed cues on the anchor sample across 5 of our mixes; broadcast sync windows (secondary sources) tolerate audio-late more than audio-early.

sources.locator: Cue anchors use the exact take; Validation

title: Level end-anchored sounds by body
statement: A sound that ends on its anchor (riser, reverse swell, suck) is levelled over its body window, not its last 8 ms fade; measured over the fade, the level solver asked for +34 dB.

title: Cap limiter gain reduction per cue
statement: Limiter gain reduction on any cue stays <= 1.5 dB for tier 1-2 and <= 1.0 dB for tier 3; when the budget is exceeded the offending cue is lowered, not the limiter.
evidence: Pack mixer contract carried over from an earlier film pipeline.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py render (limiter budget per cue) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Type-led films may open at full level
statement: A type-led launch film may skip the quiet open: put sound on by 0.25 s at 0 to -2.5 dB against the body.
evidence: 3 of 3 tier-A video films in round 9 open at -0.1 to -2.4 dB against the body with sound on by 0.25 s; the only quiet open (-18.1 dB) is the tier-C manifesto.

title: Peak the mix on the result
statement: The mix's loudest moment lands on the approved or result state change, not on the logo.
evidence: Round-7 film 12 (tier C) peaks at about -6 dB on the 4 Hz curve at 16-16.5 s of 30 s, exactly on the approving-to-approved change.

title: End every master in a true-peak limiter
statement: Every master path ends in a true-peak limiter (4x oversampled, ceiling -1.5 dBTP); a peak-gain-only ceiling lets dense cues stop the mix short of target (measured -17.49 LUFS-I at a -2.0 dBTP ceiling, 3.5 LU low).
evidence: The 3D film-scene mix stopped at -17.49 LUFS-I (delivered -17.55 at both aspects) because its mix hit the -2.0 dBTP ceiling first with no limiter.

title: Mute open when silence is the before
statement: When silence is the 'before' state, the clip opens on true silence under a mute chip for about 3 s, and the first sound lands on the same frame as the chip flip and the first action.
evidence: One proof clip of a 1.8M-view launch thread (tier B by rule, read as C) opens on 2.9 s of true silence; the sound arrives at 2.93 s with the chip flip.

title: No unplanned silence over 2 s
statement: No unplanned stretch of 2 s or more sits 20 dB or more under the programme median; anything longer is either planned in plan.audio.quiet or filled.
evidence: House default in ears; on the pack's trailer bed the unmarked file warns dead air at exactly the two intended regions and passes once they are planned.

title: Never double the score's hits
statement: When the score already carries braams and a title hit, no SFX doubles them.
evidence: Film lane recipe rule.

title: Zero renderer 'audio lowered' lines
statement: The render log shows zero 'Audio lowered' lines: the master reaches the renderer with its encoded (AAC) true peak under -1 dBTP, because the renderer's guard otherwise drops the whole track (measured 7.3 and 8.6 dB).
evidence: Two explainer-family templates mixed to -14.0 LUFS-I (WAV TP -2.35 and -3.9 dBTP) were delivered at -22.75 and -21.46 LUFS-I after the renderer's true-peak guard lowered them; the proof demo render with 0 lowered lines delivered -14.2 LUFS-I.

title: Give the mix a drop
statement: The mix is not flat: it has a level step of at least 3 dB, or LRA of 2 LU or more, or half-second levels spread more than 2 dB (P90-P10); the drop does not first arrive after 75% of the runtime.
evidence: ears on our own files: 3 of our shorts/ads held one level end to end (LRA 0.7-1.9 LU) and got the flat warning; the films with an arc passed.

title: One sub hit on the reveal
statement: A device reveal gets exactly one sub hit on the reveal frame, the dark-open hum stops on that frame, and each callout or spec row gets a detent, never a chime per row.
evidence: Hardware lane recipe; the template test asserts one sub hit per plan.
notes: Tools that touch it today: templates/_hw/hw.test.mjs (one sub hit, the drop on the reveal bar). | The test covers pack templates only; the hum stop uses cue untilT (templates/_shared/audio.py).

title: One sound per UI action

title: Cut slightly before the onset
statement: Cuts land 1-4 frames (about 49-76 ms) before the nearest audio onset.
evidence: Median cut-to-onset gaps of -64 ms (round-8 film 06, tier A small sample), -49 ms (film 03, boosted-looking) and -76 ms (film 05, tier C); film 04 (tier C) is +17 ms.

notes: Resolved 21 Oct: not a contradiction: F+1 (sound one frame after picture) is the lower edge of the measured 1-4 frame picture-leads window; the pack keeps F+1 as the testable default, accepts F+1..F+4, and never lets sound lead picture. | The onset detector has its own latency: measure our renders with the same tool before changing the pack's one-frame rule. | Merged: Sound may trail its picture event but never lead it: audio-late up to about 125 ms (about 3.75 frames at 30 fps) sits inside the ITU-R BT.1359 detectability window, while audio-early is detected from about 45 ms, so any offset beyond the F+1 contract should be late (1-4 frames), never early. The settled pack value is F+1 exactly; this rule records the wider tolerance as the alternative.

evidence: House maxima tuned on synthetic fixtures and the pack's trailer bed (a 6 s hold passes, an 11 s hold warns); thresholds are starting values, not set from a corpus of real films.

title: Never repeat the same take
statement: A repeated cue id uses seed = base + occurrence with pitch +-3% and gain +-1.5 dB (timing unchanged); the same non-musical sound more than 3 times in 10 s, or the same id 3+ times within 8 events, is flagged.
evidence: Pack rule against the machine-gun effect in typing, footsteps and ticks; mixer round-robins seeds; foley ships 4 takes per sound.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py (seed + occurrence) (a pack default outside mp plan). | ears treats a repeated plan id as a note up to 6 in 10 s because the mixer already varies takes; mixer lint_cues R9 flags 3+ in 8 events.

title: Whole-bar risers end one frame early
statement: A riser lasts a whole number of bars (1, 2 or 4; bars x 4 x 60 / BPM) and ends at the hit anchor minus 1 frame (33 ms at 30 fps) with a hard 5 ms fade-out, so the hit lands on the next downbeat after a one-frame gap.
evidence: Pack contract (manifest anchor_frame_offset = -1 on every riser); not measured for reach.
notes: Set today by: music/mixer.py (risers placed one frame earlier) (a pack default outside mp plan). | ears/sync checks the end offset; the whole-bar length is a library default (1-, 2-, 4-bar risers at 120 BPM), not checked. | Merged: A riser ends one frame before its hit, the impact lands on the frame of the visual change or up to 1 frame late (never early), and any offset over 1 frame is flagged. [house; Practitioner sound-design guidance (a transition a frame late reads as a mistake) set as the pack's house rule R1.] | A reverse swell or reverse braam ends ON the hit, not one frame before.

title: Room tone under every cut
statement: In a talking-head or dialogue edit, removed dead air is bridged with 40-80 ms of room tone (about -48 dBFS) under every cut so the cut is never a digital hole; a short film runs room tone under every shot.
evidence: Editing practice; not measured by us.
notes: For film-like silence that is not digital zero, the library has a quieter air bed (about -56 dBFS).

title: 200-400 ms silence before the turn

title: Silence before a press or swap
statement: Short silences of 0.3-2.0 s sit right before a button press, a card swap or a typing run.

title: Drop the bed under the name
statement: The bed drops to about -50 dB for 1.5 s under the product name at 85-89% of the runtime, then returns for the tagline.
evidence: The only tier-A VO film of round 7 (37.8 s) is the only VO film that stops the bed under the name (32.0-33.5 s).

title: Silent loops can carry saves
statement: A loop of 16 s or less that is meant to be saved may ship with no audio track.
evidence: Two saves-strong (A-) pieces had no audio: a 16 s round-5 loop (1.31% bookmarks) and a 14.5 s round-3 page flythrough (1.9% bookmarks).

evidence: The round-7 hardware film (tier A*, claim-driven flag) ends at +1.0 dB against the body; round-8 films 06 and 07 (tier A, small samples) also slam out.

title: Speech 10 dB over music
statement: In the 300 Hz-3.4 kHz band, speech sits at least 10 dB over the music (5-10 dB warns).

title: Use J and L cuts for bridges
statement: A J cut starts the next scene's audio 200-800 ms (default 400 ms) before its picture and an L cut lets the previous audio run 200-1200 ms (default 600 ms) over the new picture, each with an 80 ms crossfade; a short-film scene change leads the picture by 12-24 frames.
evidence: Editing practice; the 12-24 frame film lead comes from the short-film bundle, the J/L ranges are pack defaults.
notes: Talking-head B-roll inverts it: the picture leads the voice line by 150 ms (cuts/split/broll_lead). Short films use no whoosh transitions. | Merged: A J cut leads the next picture's audio by 400 ms (200-800), an L cut lets the last audio linger 600 ms (200-1200), both with an 80 ms audio crossfade and a 1.5 s room-tone bridge; short-film scene changes lead by 12-24 frames (600 ms). [craft; Widely described editing technique (practitioner guides, editing-textbook summaries); the offsets are house defaults.] | Parts cuts/split/L and cuts/split/film_J. Skip J/L in 6-15 s ads under a single music bed. J/L cuts are exempt from the SFX-per-cut rule.

title: Count sync only above chance
statement: Report cut or motion sync as share against its chance level (the fraction of the timeline inside the 2-frame onset windows) and call it sync only at z >= 2; a raw 40-65% share on a busy track is near chance.
evidence: Measured on five of the pack's local films (not references): only the cut-on-beat edit reads above chance (0.94 vs 0.53, z 3.4); four others sit near chance (0.38-0.67 vs 0.35-0.64).

statement: Every transition, punch-in or emphasis cut has a paired cue on the cut frame (about -4 dB), with at least 80% coverage of non-exempt cuts; dialogue cuts, J/L cuts, on-beat hard cuts and loop seams are exempt.
evidence: Practitioner sound-design guidance (whoosh peaks on the cut, impacts on the highest-energy frame) turned into a house coverage target ([H] 80%).
